title: Selecting the product for a generic-name prescription with no manufacturer specified under 247 CMR 9.05(2)
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.05(2), upon receiving a prescription for a generic name drug product with no manufacturer specified by the prescriber, a pharmacist may select, regardless of whether or not the prescriber has marked 'no substitution' on the prescription, any legally marketed drug product whether or not it appears in the Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drugs, in accordance with the prescriber's intent and the normal exercise of professional judgment.
exam_relevance: Tests that a generic-name prescription with no manufacturer specified leaves the choice among legally marketed products to the prescriber's intent and the pharmacist's professional judgment, that a 'no substitution' mark does not narrow that choice, and that the product need not appear in the MLID.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, interchangeable drugs

exceptions: The selection is made in accordance with the prescriber's intent and the normal exercise of professional judgment.
247 CMR 9.05(3)(e) provides that 247 CMR 9.05 shall only apply to prescriptions dispensed by a pharmacy with a Drug Store Pharmacy License.
common_confusions: Reading a 'no substitution' mark on a generic-name prescription with no manufacturer specified as fixing a manufacturer. 247 CMR 9.05(2) applies regardless of whether the prescriber has marked 'no substitution'.
Confining the choice to products in the MLID. The paragraph reaches any legally marketed drug product whether or not it appears in the list.
Applying the paragraph where the prescriber has specified a manufacturer. It is written for a generic name drug product with no manufacturer specified.
verification_notes: Read in the current 247 CMR 9.00 published on mass.gov (page footers dated 12/6/24) on 2026-09-16.
